steps_walked.title: Sources: judging switches a source on, the admission audit and its Undo, the shipped-verdict editor, and one collecting count everywhere (agent-run walk)
prerequisites: WHO RUNS IT: a Claude Code session or workflow agent in this sandbox, not the maintainer (his 2026-09-26 17:23Z message delegates the click-through). It needs the repo at /home/user/Open-Omniscience on main (checked at 462145c, which includes #1158, #1159 and #1173), the repo's .venv (Python 3.13, Playwright installed), and the pinned Chromium at /opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome. Everything runs on 127.0.0.1 and no step needs the network. $SCRATCH below means the running session's own scratchpad directory.

A DISPOSABLE COPY TO SERVE FROM, so the shared checkout is never written. Run: mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/oo-app" && git -C /home/user/Open-Omniscience archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$SCRATCH/oo-app". git archive only reads the repo. The overlay file written in S7 goes into $SCRATCH/oo-app/configs/, because the app reads configs/source_qualification.yml next to the src/ it serves.

A THROWAWAY DATA FOLDER, pre-seeded with the retired hatch. Run: mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/oo-rowS-data" && printf '{"scrape_unqualified": true}\n' > "$SCRATCH/oo-rowS-data/scheduler_settings.json". Do this BEFORE seeding. It simulates an install upgraded with the old 'also scrape unqualified sources' switch on; the app migrates the file into its settings store and must disclose the retirement.

SEED IT with the row's own walk seed, never scripts/ui_clickthrough_seed.py, which writes verdicts directly and leaves the audit empty. Run: cd /home/user/Open-Omniscience && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 OO_DATA_DIR="$SCRATCH/oo-rowS-data" OO_DB_PLAINTEXT=1 OO_NO_SCHEDULER=1 OO_AUTOSEED=0 .venv/bin/python docs/audit/sources-admission-clickthrough-2026-09-18/seed.py. It must print 'collecting: 3', 'admission events: 3 (undone 1)' and 'unaccounted: 2 of 3 collecting'. If it does not, stop: every number below assumes this seed.

BOOT the throwaway from the copy, in the background, and keep the PID: cd "$SCRATCH/oo-app" && OO_DATA_DIR="$SCRATCH/oo-rowS-data" OO_DB_PLAINTEXT=1 OO_NO_SCHEDULER=1 OO_AUTOSEED=0 OO_LLM_AUTOSTART=0 /home/user/Open-Omniscience/.venv/bin/uvicorn src.api.main:app --app-dir "$SCRATCH/oo-app" --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8213. Stop it later by PID, never pkill -f. OO_AUTOSEED=0 also skips the startup adoption of shipped verdicts, which is why S7 can show the editor with 0 in force. OO_NO_SCHEDULER=1 means the app boots ONLINE (the boot airplane engage is skipped), so S1 turns airplane mode on first.

DRIVER RULES (Playwright, one browser context, 1440×1000). Use real page/locator clicks on visible controls, never el.click() or DOM edits. Change language ONLY through the top-bar menu (#lang-switch, then the native-name item), never OOI18N.setLang. Reload after every language change except the S4 probe. Register a dialog handler (dismiss once, accept once) for Revert. Use expect_download for Export and Merge. Capture every console error and pageerror. Screenshot each step. Write a report.json in the style of the 2026-09-18 walk. Never press: 'Qualify the backlog', the first-run guide's 'Go online & start collecting', or the airplane button while it is offline (that would go online).

steps.where: http://127.0.0.1:8213 → top bar, airplane button (#net-toggle) → left sidebar, Settings (bottom button) → Advanced (subtab, #set-subtabs) → click the collapsed row "Quality gates — what counts as an article, what counts as a working source, and what gets scraped" (details[data-adv=qualification], #qualification-panel)
steps.do:
1. Open the app. If the first-run guide opens, close it with its × ("Close", #gw-close). If the airplane coachmark shows, press "Not now".
2. Click the airplane button once to go OFFLINE. Going offline needs no consent popup.
3. Go to Settings → Advanced. Before expanding anything, read #qual-state. Then expand "Quality gates".
4. Hover each of the four numbers in the line under "Judge sources automatically" and read the shared hover bubble (#oo-tip).
5. Read "What the source gate looks at" and "What gets scraped".
6. Expand the "Collection" and "Sources" sections too, and search the whole Advanced page for any control that offers to scrape unqualified or unjudged sources.
7. Tick nothing.
steps.expect:
(a) Airplane mode is on: the toast reads "Offline — every new network request is refused. One in-flight request may finish." and #net-plane has fill="currentColor" (filled).
(b) Before expanding, #qual-state still reads "Loading…": the section fetches nothing until opened.
(c) After expanding, the headline reads exactly "Collecting now: 3 · Judged so far: 4 qualified · 2 disqualified · 5 not yet judged". The hover bubbles read, in order:
- 3: "enabled AND qualified — what collection actually reaches. This is the headline figure; every other count below answers a different question."
- 4: "qualified, whether or not enabled — a verdict, not a collection state"
- 2: "judged and found wanting, whether or not enabled"
- 5: "not yet judged, whether or not enabled"
(d) "What the source gate looks at" lists six criteria: outlier_rate, pathology_rate, link_density_rate, furniture_share, language_mismatch_rate, short_article_rate. Exactly two read "can disqualify": pathology_rate with "· absolute floor: 0.5", and link_density_rate with "· no absolute floor". The other four read "watch only". Below the list, visible without hovering, an amber line begins "Kept as a rare-catastrophe detector. It has never fired in the field".
(e) "What gets scraped" has exactly one checkbox, "Only scrape the sources that came with the app" (unticked), under "A source is scraped once it is enabled and has passed judging. Passing judging enables it…". The line under it reads "This will scrape 3 sources (of 6 enabled)." An amber line (#qual-scope-retired, not hidden) begins "The 'also scrape unqualified sources' setting has been retired (ruling Q1101, 2026-09-15)." It ends by pointing to "Settings > Sources > Admission audit", a path that does not exist: record that as finding F5. If the amber line is missing, read GET /api/sources/qualification/config → scope.retired to tell "not stored" apart from "not rendered", and record which.
(f) No checkbox or toggle anywhere under Advanced offers to scrape unqualified or unjudged sources.

verdicts.title: F3: 'Build a merged file' never shows the server's refusal ('Merging…' sticks, TypeError); Export's YAML is not accepted by Merge
verdicts.reason: I reproduced this on my own locked, encrypted instance (port 8844, console script, airplane mode on, 1440px, en). Export saved source_qualification.yml, which is YAML. With that file in #qual-ov-files, pressing 'Build a merged file' downloaded nothing. #qual-ov-merge-out still read 'Merging…' 16 s later, a pageerror "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'status')" fired, and the POST got a 400. I also tried a file the picker DOES accept: not-an-export.json containing {"hello":"world"}. It stuck the same way, with the same TypeError. So this is reachable without choosing 'All files'. The server's own replies are readable and never appear: 'not-an-export.json: no 'verdicts' list -- is this a source-qualification export?' and '...yml: not valid JSON (...)'. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/S-recheck/shots/S-F3-merge-json-stuck-en.png, S-F3-merge-yaml-stuck-en.png and raw_recheck.json steps.F3_merge. The YAML-versus-JSON half is a design gap rather than a defect in itself. The export endpoint's docstring says fmt=yaml is 'the overlay file itself, ready to commit', while Merge reads the JSON export or an all-diagnostics zip, and the picker's accept='.json,.zip' says so. The gap is that the panel offers no JSON export, even though its merge sentence says 'merge exports from other instances'. The YAML header's pointer to scripts/merge_source_qualification.py is still true, because the script remains a second entry point to the same code. Severity: P2 is kept. No data is at risk, but every refusal from this maintainer tool is swallowed and leaves a permanent 'Merging…'.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-ai-tools.js:473 throws a plain `new Error(detail)`, and :496 passes it to `_apiErrorMessage(e)`. That Error has no `.detail`, so src/static/app-core.js:2513 falls back to `res.status` with `res` undefined, and the catch block itself throws a TypeError. overlayExport has the same shape (app-ai-tools.js:441 then :444), so an export failure would also crash its catch without a toast. The helper has about 20 single-argument callers that pass an Error. Every one of them crashes the same way whenever api() rejects with no `detail`, for example a 500 with a plain-text body.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Smallest broad fix: make the helper tolerate a missing res. At app-core.js:2513 use `return msg || (res ? res.status + " " + res.statusText : (data && data.message) || String(data));`. That repairs overlayMerge, overlayExport and the other single-argument callers in one line. Separately, as a follow-up and not required for this defect: either let rows_from_export_bytes (src/catalog/qualification_merge.py) accept the YAML overlay via yaml.safe_load, since it carries the same verdict rows, or add a JSON export next to Export and say which file Merge takes.
